name: prehistoric_disasters
style_suffix: cinematic prehistoric disaster documentary, epic natural catastrophe, dark and high-contrast, desaturated ash-grey, bone, and ember-orange palette, vast overwhelming scale, a tiny lone human silhouette dwarfed by the catastrophe for scale, deep shadow, volumetric haze and falling ash, photoreal, dramatic and ominous, weathered primeval earth, no text, no modern elements, 16:9
default_music_prompt: Slow, ominous deep-time documentary underscore. Low sustained drones, sub-bass swells, sparse distant percussion like settling earth, a thread of cold tension. Vast, dreadful, patient. No melody that competes with a narrator. Builds slow grandeur and unease, then holds.
default_motion: slow, gentle drift and push-in only; restrained minimal motion (this channel builds Ken-Burns-only — Kling beat count 0 at launch)

thumbnail.candidate_prompt_suffix: YouTube thumbnail composition, strongly asymmetric: the single overwhelming catastrophe (towering ash column / wildfire sky / tidal wall / supervolcano plume) is massed in the RIGHT TWO-THIRDS of the frame; the LEFT THIRD is deliberately dark, empty, shadowed, low-detail negative space reserved for a headline; one small human silhouette stands LOW and RIGHT-OF-CENTRE directly beneath the towering catastrophe so the terrifying scale reads at a glance; high-contrast, deep shadow, the catastrophe brightly lit against the dark left; single subject only, no clutter, no text, no letters
selection_rules: ONE overwhelming catastrophe that reads instantly at phone-thumbnail size
maximum dark, high-contrast cinematic drama — it must stand out in a dim feed
an unmistakable TINY human silhouette low in the frame giving terrifying scale
clean, darker, uncluttered negative space in the TOP-LEFT where the headline lands
no garbled detail, no accidental letterforms, no duplicated or broken figures, one subject only
